steps: Write down the oven settings: 425F, 25 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 425 minus 25 is 400F, and the time stays 25 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 25 × 0.75 = 18.75, rounded to 19 minutes, at the same 425F.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For frozen foods at 425F for 25 minutes: either 400F for 25 minutes, or 425F and check at about 19 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the package
howToSteps.text: Find the oven temperature and time on the bag or box. Frozen fries usually say 425F for 25 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick one change
howToSteps.text: Pick one change, not both. Either take 25F off the temperature and keep the time, or keep the temperature and check a quarter sooner. 425F for 25 minutes becomes either 400F for 25 minutes or 425F and check at about 19 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Load straight from the freezer
howToSteps.text: No thawing, no oil. Spread the food in a single layer so the hot air reaches every piece.

howToSteps.name: Shake and check early
howToSteps.text: Shake halfway through. Pull the food when it is golden and hot through.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Frozen Foods
tutorial: Frozen food is the best job for an air fryer, because it goes straight from the freezer to the basket with no thawing and no prep. A bag of fries that bakes at 425F for 25 minutes air fries two ways: 400F for the full 25 minutes, or 425F and check at about 19 minutes.

The package directions are your starting point, and this converter translates them. Read the oven temperature and time off the bag or the box, convert one of the two numbers, and cook. The package knows the food better than any chart does, and the converted settings keep what the package knows while fitting the faster machine.

One thing is different for frozen food. Frozen food needs the heat to thaw and cook at once, so the shorter-time option suits it well: keep the oven temperature and check about a quarter sooner. The lower-temperature option works too, with the full oven time. If the first batch comes out pale, use the shorter-time option next time.

No oil, no thawing, no preheating debate. Frozen food already holds the oil it needs, so it crisps with nothing added. A preheat helps for a short cook, and matters less for a long one, because the food warms up with the basket either way.

One exception matters more than any time on this page. Raw, stuffed, breaded chicken breast products should not be cooked in an air fryer at all. The breading browns before the filling is safe, and the package instructions are written for an oven for a reason. Follow the package for those, every time.
